title: Certified small firms beside larger firms in the contract notices (checked)
question: Does a certified local or disadvantaged firm give the same telephone, email domain or suite as a much larger uncertified City payee that the directory does not list as its affiliate?
finding: 1,175 certified firm names (the City's local-business directory and the State directory for five Bay Area counties) were set against 1,725 contractor names on contract notices and against the business registry. None shares a telephone or email domain with a larger uncertified City payee beyond the affiliates the directory itself records. 16 pairings rest on a suite alone, each in an office that other registered businesses also use.
how: Telephones, company email domains and suite-level addresses of every firm in the City Partner local-business directory and the California Unified Certification Program directory (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, San Francisco and San Mateo counties) are compared exactly with those typed on City contract notices and with suites in the Treasurer's business registry. A pairing is kept when the other name is not certified, is not among the firm's recorded participation-credit restrictions, was paid at least $2 million since fiscal 2019 and at least three times what the certified firm was paid.
limits: This adds the contract notices and the State directory to the test the “lbe fronts” analysis already ran on the registry; it found nothing new of weight. A shared suite in a multi-tenant office or business centre is ordinary, and the column "others registered at the suite" shows how crowded each is. The directories are today's lists and cannot test past certifications.
